sections.overview: The palm cockatoo is a large parrot and the sole living species in its genus, Probosciger.
sections.identification: Its mostly black plumage, tall crest and bare red cheek patches make it distinctive among parrots.
sections.habitat: It inhabits forest, wooded savanna and riparian habitats in northern Australia and New Guinea.
sections.diet: Its diet is mainly plant-based, including seeds, nuts, fruits and buds; it also takes insects.
sections.behavior: Males may shape a stick or seedpod and drum it against a hollow tree during display.
sections.reproduction: It nests in large tree hollows and typically lays a single egg; breeding is unusually infrequent for a parrot.
sections.ecology: Its dependence on large nesting hollows makes the retention of old hollow-bearing trees important to its breeding habitat.
sections.conservation: BirdLife elevated the global status to Near Threatened in 2023, citing habitat loss and trapping pressure.
